cls: Antineoplastic - third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor
pharm: Irreversible inhibitor of mutant epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), including sensitizing mutations (exon 19 deletions, L858R) and the T790M resistance mutation, with relative sparing of wild-type EGFR; used in EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer.
quick: Take with or without food at the same time each day
Can cause fetal harm; avoid - use effective contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for 2 weeks after the last dose
No adjustment in mild-moderate; limited data in severe/ESRD
No adjustment in mild-moderate; not studied in severe
No specific interaction; limit due to additive effects
LVEF/ECG (QTc), pulmonary symptoms (ILD), CBC, pregnancy status
summary: Osimertinib is a third-generation, irreversible oral EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor used to treat EGFR mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It is active against common sensitizing EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletions and exon 21 L858R) and against the T790M resistance mutation, while relatively sparing wild-type EGFR, which lessens skin and GI toxicity compared with earlier EGFR-TKIs. Approved uses include first-line treatment of metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC, treatment of T790M-positive NSCLC after progression on prior EGFR-TKI therapy, adjuvant therapy after tumor resection in EGFR-mutated NSCLC, and (combined with chemotherapy) first-line metastatic disease, plus unresectable stage III disease after chemoradiation. The standard dose is 80 mg once daily. Important serious risks include interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, QTc prolongation, cardiomyopathy with decreased left ventricular ejection fraction, keratitis, erythema multiforme/Stevens-Johnson syndrome, aplastic anemia, and embryo-fetal toxicity. It is a CYP3A substrate; strong CYP3A inducers reduce exposure.
indications: First-line treatment of metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations
Treatment of metastatic EGFR T790M mutation-positive NSCLC with progression on or after EGFR-TKI therapy
Adjuvant treatment after tumor resection of EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation-positive NSCLC
First-line treatment of locally advanced/metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy
Treatment of locally advanced, unresectable (stage III) EGFR-mutated NSCLC without progression during or after chemoradiation

dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; for adjuvant use treat for up to 3 years
Reduce after interruption for adverse reactions; discontinue if not tolerated at 40 mg

dosage.d: Disperse tablet in ~60 mL (4 tablespoons) of non-carbonated water
dosage.n: Stir, drink immediately, rinse container with water and drink; do not crush, heat, or use other liquids

dosage.d: 160 mg once daily (if strong inducer cannot be avoided)
dosage.n: Resume 80 mg 3 weeks after discontinuing the inducer; avoid strong inducers where possible

admin: Take one tablet by mouth once daily, with or without food, at approximately the same time each day
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush, split, or chew
For patients unable to swallow, disperse the tablet in about 60 mL of non-carbonated water only, stir until dispersed, and drink immediately, then rinse and drink residue
If a dose is missed by more than ~12 hours, skip it and take the next dose at the scheduled time
Obtain baseline and periodic ECG and assess LVEF; monitor for pulmonary, cardiac, and dermatologic toxicity
moa: Osimertinib is a third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor that binds irreversibly (covalently) to a cysteine residue (C797) in the ATP-binding site of certain mutant forms of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). It potently and selectively inhibits EGFR bearing sensitizing mutations (exon 19 deletions and exon 21 L858R) and the T790M resistance mutation, while having substantially lower activity against wild-type EGFR. By blocking EGFR autophosphorylation and downstream signaling (RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK and PI3K/AKT pathways), it inhibits tumor cell proliferation and survival in EGFR-mutant NSCLC. Two active circulating metabolites (AZ5104 and AZ7550) contribute to activity. Its relative sparing of wild-type EGFR underlies a comparatively lower incidence of rash and diarrhea than earlier EGFR-TKIs.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to osimertinib or any excipient
relative: History or risk of QT prolongation (congenital long QT, electrolyte abnormalities, other QT-prolonging drugs)
Cardiac dysfunction or risk factors for reduced LVEF/heart failure
Prior or active interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis
monitor: Pulmonary symptoms for interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis
ECG for QTc prolongation and electrolytes (potassium, magnesium)
Skin and mucosa for erythema multiforme/Stevens-Johnson syndrome and ophthalmic symptoms (keratitis)
Complete blood count for aplastic anemia/cytopenias

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal findings, osimertinib can cause fetal harm including embryolethality and malformations. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and for 6 weeks after the last dose. Males with female partners of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 months after the final dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of osimertinib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 2 weeks after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild to moderate renal impairment. There are limited data in severe renal impairment and no data in end-stage renal disease; use with caution and monitor closely.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild (Child-Pugh A) or moderate (Child-Pugh B) hepatic impairment. Osimertinib has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C); use with caution if at all.

major: Strong CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, St John's wort) - significantly reduce osimertinib exposure; avoid, or if unavoidable increase dose to 160 mg daily
QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., antiarrhythmics, certain antipsychotics, methadone, some antibiotics) - additive risk of QT prolongation and torsades; avoid or monitor ECG closely
Sensitive BCRP or P-gp substrates with narrow therapeutic index (e.g., rosuvastatin) - osimertinib may increase their exposure; monitor
moderate: Drugs that lower potassium/magnesium (diuretics) - worsen QT risk; correct electrolytes
Other agents associated with pneumonitis or cardiotoxicity - additive organ toxicity
minor: Strong CYP3A inhibitors had no clinically meaningful effect on exposure - no dose change needed
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no clinically significant food effect.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol due to additive constitutional effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor ECG (QTc) and serum electrolytes; assess LVEF by echocardiography or MUGA at baseline and periodically; monitor blood counts.

serious: QTc prolongation and torsades de pointes
Cardiomyopathy with decreased left ventricular ejection fraction / heart failure
emergency: New or worsening cough, dyspnea, or fever (pneumonitis)
Syncope, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation/arrhythmia)
Symptoms of heart failure (breathlessness, edema, fatigue)
Severe blistering/peeling skin rash or mucosal involvement (SJS/erythema multiforme)
Severe bleeding, bruising, or infection (aplastic anemia)

monitoring: Pulmonary symptoms; withhold and evaluate for ILD/pneumonitis, and permanently discontinue if confirmed
ECG and electrolytes (potassium, magnesium) for QTc prolongation, especially with risk factors or QT-prolonging drugs
Assessment of left ventricular ejection fraction at baseline and periodically in patients with cardiac risk factors
Skin and mucous membranes for severe cutaneous reactions; ophthalmologic evaluation for new or worsening eye symptoms
Complete blood count; pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential
counsel: Take one tablet once a day, with or without food, at about the same time; swallow whole or disperse only in plain water if you cannot swallow it
If you miss a dose and it has been less than 12 hours, take it; otherwise skip it and take the next dose on time - do not double up
Report any new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or fever right away (possible lung inflammation)
Tell your team about fainting, palpitations, swelling of the legs, or worsening breathlessness (heart rhythm or heart muscle effects)
Report severe rash, blistering, mouth sores, or new eye pain/vision changes promptly
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed; tell your doctor about all other medicines, especially those affecting heart rhythm
pk: Antitumor responses develop over weeks; target inhibition is sustained with daily dosing
Median plasma Tmax ~6 hours after oral dosing
Steady state reached in approximately 15 days with once-daily dosing
pearls: Third-generation EGFR-TKI active against both sensitizing mutations AND the T790M resistance mutation, with relative wild-type EGFR sparing (less rash/diarrhea than earlier TKIs)
Cardiac toxicity: monitor QTc/electrolytes and assess LVEF - withhold or discontinue for symptomatic heart failure or marked LVEF decline
ILD/pneumonitis can be fatal - withhold for any new respiratory symptoms and permanently discontinue if pneumonitis is confirmed
Watch for severe cutaneous reactions (erythema multiforme, SJS), keratitis (urgent ophthalmology referral), and rare aplastic anemia
CYP3A substrate - avoid strong inducers; if unavoidable, increase dose to 160 mg daily and revert to 80 mg three weeks after stopping the inducer
Embryo-fetal toxicity - confirm contraception during and for 6 weeks (females) / 4 months (males) after treatment; do not breastfeed
missed: If you miss a dose of osimertinib and it has been less than about 12 hours, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If more than 12 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific treatment for osimertinib overdose. Symptoms are not well defined but may reflect exaggerated adverse effects. Manage with supportive care, including cardiac monitoring (ECG for QT prolongation) and correction of electrolyte abnormalities, and monitor for pulmonary, cardiac, and hematologic toxicity.
